description: Field-level definition of every annotation ClauseXplain adds on top of Phase 1's CUAD-derived, category-mapped spans. Fields carried over unchanged from Phase 1 are marked source='phase1_carryover'. All other fields are NEW in Phase 2 and, until a human or documented rule-based process actually populates them, MUST be null -- never a fabricated default.

fields.name: clause_id
fields.description: Unique ID from Phase 1, format {contract_id}__{cuad_category}__{span_index}.

fields.name: contract_id
fields.description: Foreign key into contracts.csv.

fields.name: cuad_category
fields.description: Original CUAD category name, one of 41. Never overwritten.

fields.name: clausexplain_category
fields.description: Mapped target category from category_mapping.csv. Null for METADATA/EXCLUDED rows.

fields.name: category_status
fields.description: Whether this span was mapped to a risk category, is structural metadata, or was excluded.

fields.name: clause_text
fields.description: The CUAD-highlighted span text. NOTE: this may be a partial excerpt, not necessarily a complete self-contained clause -- see span_type.

fields.name: span_type
fields.description: Deliberately not called 'clause' -- CUAD spans are expert-highlighted excerpts, not guaranteed to be complete, self-contained clauses.

fields.name: needs_review
fields.description: True if the category mapping itself (Phase 1) was a judgment call. Independent of Phase 2's own review flags below.

fields.name: risk_level
fields.description: Overall discretized risk level, derived from risk_score using ClauseXplain's proposed operational thresholds (see risk_scoring_specification.txt). NOT a legal determination. Null until an annotator or documented rule assigns it.

fields.name: risk_score
fields.description: Weighted combination of the five risk-dimension scores below. Null until computed from actual non-null dimension scores -- never back-filled from risk_level.

fields.name: unfairness_score
fields.description: Degree to which the clause imposes asymmetric or one-sided obligations. Annotator-assigned or explicitly rule_based_preannotation; see PHASE2_ANNOTATION_GUIDELINES.txt for scoring bands.

fields.name: ambiguity_score
fields.description: Degree to which the clause's language is vague, undefined, or open to multiple reasonable interpretations.

fields.name: non_compliance_score
fields.description: Degree to which the clause appears to conflict with a specific Indian statutory provision (see legal_provision field). Must trace to an actual entry in indian_legal_rules.csv, not intuition.

fields.name: precedent_match_score
fields.description: Similarity to a known risky clause pattern. NOTE: at this stage ClauseXplain has no curated precedent/case-law corpus; this field remains null for all records until such a corpus exists (see PHASE2_README.txt, 'What remains for Phase 3').

fields.name: enforceability_score
fields.description: Degree of concern that the clause, or part of it, may be unenforceable under Indian law (e.g. an overbroad restraint-of-trade clause).

fields.name: legal_risk_type
fields.description: Zero or more tags describing the nature of concern. Never 'illegal' -- that word is disallowed by design.

fields.name: indian_law_relevant
fields.description: Whether any Indian statutory provision is plausibly relevant to this clause. Null, not false, if not yet assessed.

fields.name: legal_provision
fields.description: Citation of the specific statute and section, e.g. 'Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 27'. Must match an entry in indian_legal_rules.csv.

fields.name: legal_basis
fields.description: Short plain-language explanation of why the provision may be relevant, using cautious language ('may raise issues under...', never 'violates').

fields.name: legal_confidence
fields.description: Annotator's confidence that the legal_provision citation is actually applicable to this specific clause.

fields.name: requires_legal_review
fields.description: Defaults to true for every record until a qualified legal reviewer (not currently available on this project -- see FINAL_DATASET_README.txt) signs off. This field exists specifically so no output can be mistaken for lawyer-validated content.

fields.name: annotation_source
fields.description: Provenance of every risk/legal field above. 'human_legal_expert_annotation' must never be set unless an actual qualified legal reviewer performed the annotation -- this project currently has none, so this value should not appear anywhere in Phase 2 output.

fields.name: annotation_confidence
fields.description: Annotator's overall confidence in the full annotation record, distinct from legal_confidence which is specific to the legal_provision citation.

fields.name: annotator_id
fields.description: Identifier of the human annotator, or 'rule_engine_v1' for rule-based preannotation. Null if not yet annotated.

fields.name: annotation_timestamp
fields.description: When the annotation was made. Null if not yet annotated.

notes: risk_level and risk_score are DERIVED fields: they must never be set directly without the five underlying dimension scores also being present and non-null, since risk_score is defined as a function of them.

annotation_source is the single most important field for research integrity in this schema -- every downstream statistic must be reported conditional on this field, e.g. 'X records are rule_based_preannotation, Y are not_yet_annotated, Z are human_researcher_annotation' rather than a single aggregate number.

As of Phase 2 completion, annotation_source='human_legal_expert_annotation' does not appear anywhere in the dataset. If it appears in a future version, it must correspond to an actual named reviewer, documented in a separate annotator log -- never inferred.
